title: Dzaleka refugee camp trafficking network (Malawi)
summary: UNODC and the Malawi Police Service report that a trafficking network used the Dzaleka Refugee Camp, 41 km from Lilongwe, as a hub. Agents in Ethiopia, the DRC and Burundi recruited people under false pretences, offering work in South Africa, and arranged their crossing into Malawi and entry into the camp; there they were told to pay off debts for being smuggled and were exploited in the camp or moved on for forced labour. Children were exploited for farm and domestic work and women and girls for sexual exploitation, in the camp, in Malawi and elsewhere in Southern Africa. After UNODC training, over 90 victims were identified and rescued, most of them Ethiopian men aged 18–30. As of May 2022 there were five arrests of suspects from Malawi, Ethiopia, Burundi, Rwanda and the DRC and cases were ongoing; police said victims' fear of testifying was hampering convictions. No one is named.
